clue.text: Chamber containing stolen picture

indicators.note: the chamber word holds the stolen word inside it, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a po is a chamber pot
hot is slang for stolen goods

explanation.surface: A thief hides a stolen painting inside a room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chamber' looks like a room, but po is informal British for a chamber pot; 'stolen' is the slang hot, as in hot goods.
explanation.definitionFit: A snapshot is a picture taken with a camera.

clue.text: Loyal father given a lot of credit, supporting three

indicators.note: in a down answer the piece that supports another is written beneath it

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
a trio is a group of three

indicators.note: most but not all of the credit word is used, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: tick is British slang for credit, as in buying on tick

explanation.surface: A dad who is given a generous loan while backing a trio of people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot of' cuts the last letter from TICK to leave TIC; 'supporting' puts it below TRIO in the down light. On tick means on credit in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A patriot is devoted to their country, so the adjective means faithful to it.

clue.text: Not concealed on time

parts.note: over can mean on, as a lid laid over a pot

explanation.surface: Something left in plain view, and punctual too.
explanation.definitionFit: Overt means open and plainly visible, the opposite of hidden.

clue.text: After wasting first of January, say, I become very active

indicators.note: wasting the opening letter means the first letter of the month word is thrown away

parts.note: January is an example of a month
the ego is the self, the I

explanation.surface: Someone who, once early January has passed, becomes a whirlwind of activity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'January, say' is MONTH; 'wasting first of' removes its M to give ONTH, followed by EGO for I.
explanation.definitionFit: Being busy and constantly moving about is an idiom for being hectic and energetic.

clue.text: Man reacts violently in baptism, say

indicators.note: a violent reaction throws the letters of these two words into disorder

explanation.surface: A man reacts wildly at a christening.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reaction of a baby or a man at a christening is a red herring: 'violently' rearranges MAN REACTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Baptism is one example of a Christian rite of this kind, hence 'say'.

clue.text: Hit on an advertising catchphrase

parts.note: to slog is to hit hard, as a batsman does

explanation.surface: Someone striking upon a clever line for an advert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is just a link word joining the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A memorable motto used in marketing is a short catchy phrase for a product.

clue.text: Horse box with security device

parts.note: a chest is a large box
a nut secures a bolt, holding parts together

explanation.surface: A horse in a stable with a lock on the door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'security device' suggests a lock, but it is the nut that fastens onto a bolt.
explanation.definitionFit: A reddish-brown horse is called by this colour name.

clue.text: Flavouring also I note has been introduced

indicators.note: the phrase is put inside the word for also, introduced into it

parts.note: and means also, in addition
I see means I note or I understand

explanation.surface: A remark that another flavour has also been added to the recipe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I note' is read as the phrase I SEE, which goes inside AND.
explanation.definitionFit: This liquorice-tasting seed of the anise plant is used to flavour food and drinks.

clue.text: Abstract poem, abridged, is included in book

indicators.note: an abridged text is shortened, so the poem word loses its final letter

parts.note: an epic is a long narrative poem

indicators.note: the little word is placed inside the book word

parts.note: a tome is a large book

explanation.surface: Someone shortening a poem for inclusion in an anthology.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abstract' here is a verb, not an adjective; the held clue lost the word 'is', which the wordplay needs inside the book.
explanation.definitionFit: To summarise or condense a text is to make a concise summary of it.

clue.text: Health food

definitions.meaning: a drink to someone's good health

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a drink raised to wish someone well and browned bread.

clue.text: Game for the majority once

definitions.meaning: a card game, also called blackjack or pontoon
majority here is the legal age of adulthood, which in Britain was formerly this age

explanation.surface: A game for older players only.
explanation.walkthrough: The age of majority in Britain was lowered to eighteen in 1969, so this was the age once; 'majority' is not 'most people'.
explanation.definitionFit: Blackjack carries a numeric name, and that number of years was formerly the legal age of adulthood.

clue.text: One taking business to a Spanish island

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
biz is informal for business, as in showbiz

explanation.surface: Someone taking their business abroad to a Balearic holiday spot.
explanation.definitionFit: This Balearic island belongs to Spain.

clue.text: Where airport transfers may finish up when all else has failed

definitions.text: Where airport transfers may finish up
definitions.meaning: a coach from the airport ends its run at the last holiday hotel on its route
an idiom for as a final option

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase literally places a coach at the final holiday hotel and idiomatically means as a final fallback.

clue.text: Counts out the letters in American city

indicators.note: out signals the letters of the word are knocked out of order

explanation.surface: Someone spelling out a US city letter by letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges COUNTS; 'the letters in' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a city in Arizona in the United States.

clue.text: You'll see me in business working mineral

definitions.text: You'll see me in business working mineral

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a business

indicators.note: working means the letters of the word are being reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: A miner speaking about his trade in the extraction industry.
explanation.walkthrough: CO plus ALMINER, the rearrangement of MINERAL signalled by 'working'; the whole clue is the speaker's description of himself.
explanation.definitionFit: A pitman digs out the black fuel mineral as his job.

clue.text: Billy is accepted by headmaster for religious teaching

parts.note: Billy Budd is Melville's novella and Britten's opera, so Billy suggests Budd

indicators.note: the little word is taken into the abbreviation for headmaster

parts.note: HM is the abbreviation for headmaster

explanation.surface: A boy called Billy is admitted to school by the head to study religion.
explanation.walkthrough: Billy Budd is the sailor of Herman Melville's story and Benjamin Britten's opera, so 'Billy' calls up that surname.
explanation.definitionFit: This faith founded on the teachings of the Buddha is a religious doctrine.

clue.text: Medicament disguised with no end of seafood in pie filling

indicators.note: disguised means the letters of the medicine word are rearranged
the final letter of the seafood word is the one taken away

explanation.surface: Medicine hidden in a seafood pie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no' removes D, the last letter of 'seafood', from MEDICAMENT; 'disguised' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: The sweet mixture of dried fruit and spice fills Christmas pies in Britain.

clue.text: Leading Roman state? Italy's first, followed by Gaul, possibly

parts.note: Cal is an abbreviation of California, a US state

indicators.note: first means take the opening letter of the country's name
possibly signals that the letters of the word may be rearranged

explanation.surface: A question about who led the Roman state: Italy first, then Gaul.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roman state' reads as one phrase but splits: 'Leading Roman' is the definition and 'state' is California's short form. 'possibly' rearranges GAUL to ULGA.
explanation.definitionFit: This was a first-century emperor, the head of Rome.

clue.text: Class liable to talk nonsense

parts.note: cl is an abbreviation for class
apt to means liable to
to rap is to talk, chat

explanation.surface: A school class that tends to talk rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Claptrap is empty, pretentious talk, i.e. rubbish.

clue.text: To sailors, trouble may be what it represents

definitions.text: To sailors, trouble may be what it represents

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy, the sailors
ado means fuss or trouble

explanation.surface: To seafarers, this is what spells trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: TO, RN for Royal Navy and ADO in a row; read whole, the clue describes the storm itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A violent whirlwind storm spells danger at sea.

clue.text: Business good — then board loses heart

parts.note: pi is short for pious, good

indicators.note: losing its heart means the middle letter of the phrase is removed

parts.note: to get on a ship or bus is to board it

explanation.surface: A firm doing well until the board loses its nerve.
explanation.walkthrough: GET ON loses its central T to give GEON. 'Business' is meant in the sense 'that's not my pigeon'.
explanation.definitionFit: In British idiom, 'not my pigeon' means not my concern or affair.

clue.text: Vet injects phosphorus into small creature

indicators.note: injecting puts something inside, here the chemical symbol goes into the creature

parts.note: an insect is a small creature
P is the chemical symbol for phosphorus

explanation.surface: An animal doctor giving a chemical jab to a tiny animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vet' looks like the animal doctor, but here it is the verb to check.
explanation.definitionFit: To vet something is to examine it carefully.

clue.text: Sally's aggrieved about it, having been upset

indicators.note: the aggrieved word goes around the other piece

parts.note: sore means aggrieved or resentful

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the word it is read backwards

explanation.surface: A woman called Sally is annoyed about something that has been knocked over.
explanation.walkthrough: Sally is not a name here but a military sortie; 'having been upset' turns the little word over before it goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A sally is a sudden charge out by besieged troops, a military foray.

clue.text: Hero in romance is unconventional, regardless of circumstances

indicators.note: unconventional means the letters of the romantic phrase are set out in an unusual order

explanation.surface: A romantic novel whose hero breaks the mould.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unconventional' rearranges all fifteen letters of HERO IN ROMANCE IS, including the 'is' that looks like the link verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase about any weather is an idiom for whatever happens.

clue.text: Jammy copper retiring

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
retiring means shy, reserved

explanation.surface: A shy policeman who has had a lucky break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jammy' is British slang for lucky or easy; 'copper' suggests a police officer but is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are British slang for easy and comfortable, a soft option.

clue.text: Hard situation showing incongruity

definitions.meaning: a state of affairs that is the opposite of what was expected

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both resembling iron and a contradiction between what is expected and what happens.

clue.text: Someone very busy at the present time

definitions.text: Someone very busy at the present time

parts.words: Someone very busy at the present time
parts.note: present time is read as gift season, when one figure delivers gifts to children

explanation.definitionFit: Father Christmas is busiest at Christmas, the season of gifts.

clue.text: Wacky flag is flown here

definitions.meaning: British slang for crazy or mad
a flag is raised on a mast

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is British slang for mad, and literally where a flag hangs on a flagpole.

clue.text: Not a short drink, obviously

parts.note: a short is a measure of spirits; this drink is a beer served in a vessel about a metre long

explanation.definitionFit: A tall glass of beer about three feet long is anything but a short tot of spirits.

clue.text: Meeting? Go by road

parts.note: a go is an attempt, a try
ST is the abbreviation for street, a road

explanation.surface: Travel by road to a rendezvous.
explanation.definitionFit: A tryst is a secret romantic rendezvous.
